applies_to: Trane Agility water-cooled chillers with Symbio 800 controls, as listed in BAS-PTS007C-EN (6/30/2026).
summary: Trane's Agility is a compact water-cooled centrifugal chiller with an adaptive-frequency drive. Its Symbio 800 controller serves BACnet and Modbus RTU/TCP from one points list. This map covers the analog inputs (setpoints, drive values, flows, temperatures, pressures, energy meter), BAS setpoints, binary status and diagnostic flags and the multi-state mode points.

addressing.note: The list prints Modicon register numbers: 3xxxx are input registers and 4xxxx holding registers, so 30011 is input register address 10 and 42011 is holding register address 2010.

source.title: Symbio 800 Integration Points List, BACnet/Modbus, Agility Water-Cooled Chillers

notes: Register format table: analog points are 32-bit floats sent high word / high byte first (NaN = invalid); binary and multi-state points are unsigned 16-bit integers (0xFFFF = invalid).
Values are sent in the unit system ordered from the factory (I-P is the usual default, SI optional); the list names only the quantity, so temperature/pressure/flow units are left blank here.
Not every point exists on every unit: the controller builds its point set from the unit's configuration. Descriptions name the configuration a point depends on.
Register numbers are printed in 5-digit Modicon form (3xxxx input registers, 4xxxx holding registers) and converted here to wire addresses (30011 = input register 10).

Agility integration guide BAS-SVP047B-EN (Sept 2023, https://elibrary.tranetechnologies.com/public/commercial-hvac/Literature/Integration/BAS-SVP047B-EN_09092023.pdf) gives the same register format and the Modbus RTU/TCP setup steps used in the integration block.
Left out: AI-10173 to AI-10184 (registers 30157-30168). The list numbers these 32-bit floats one register apart, which cannot be right for two-register values, so their true addresses are unclear.

integration.summary: Read the analog inputs as pairs of input registers (float, high word first) and the binary/multi-state points as single registers. Write the BAS setpoints and command points in the 4xxxx holding range.
integration.enable: On the Symbio 800 web interface (USB connection) go to Installation > Identification and Communications > Protocol Configuration and select Modbus RTU or Modbus TCP; for TCP set the IP address on the IP Configuration tab.
quirks: Analog values are 32-bit floats in two consecutive registers, high word first.
0xFFFF in a binary or multi-state register and NaN in an analog register mean the value is invalid.
setup: The Modbus RTU address comes from the controller's rotary dials (001-247); 000 disables Modbus RTU. A change takes effect without a power cycle.
Modbus TCP uses Ethernet port 1 (port 2 is reserved for the optional touch screen); the rotary address is not used for TCP and the Wi-Fi module does not support Modbus TCP.
gotchas: Points not supported by the unit's configuration are absent; confirm the configuration dependencies before mapping.

verified.method: independent re-check of every register against the source PDF
